opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $48M of share-based pay and $11M of related employer taxes.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +34% YoY — a quarterly record, first above $1B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $0.21 a year ago; non-GAAP $0.55

kpis.label: Remaining performance obligations
kpis.note: unearned revenue to be recognized later; ACV $1,365M, +15% YoY

oneTimers: Arm recorded a $290M loss from equity investments in the quarter, which it strips out of its non-GAAP results: excluding it (and share-based pay), non-GAAP net income was $584M versus $210M GAAP.
otherDetail: Combined other items took $266M out of profit: a $290M loss from equity investments, partly offset by $27M of net interest income less a $3M other non-operating loss. Tax was a $66M benefit — a 45.8% effective benefit rate — thanks to windfall gains and R&D tax credits.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 53% YoY on the timing and size of high-value license agreements and contributions from backlog — a record.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 18% YoY on wider use of the Armv9 architecture, the ramp of chips based on Arm CSS (ready-made compute subsystems), and more Arm-based chips in data centers.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 34% to a record $1,241M — the first time Arm has crossed $1B in a quarter. License revenue jumped 53% to a record $634M and royalty revenue rose 18% to a record $607M. For the full fiscal year, revenue was a record $4,007M, up 24%, with royalty revenue above $2B for the first time.
takeaways.title: First billion-dollar quarter

takeaways.text: Royalty revenue grew 18% to $607M on wider use of the Armv9 architecture, the ramp of Arm CSS ready-made compute subsystems, and more Arm-based chips in data centers. Smartphone royalties grew about 30% even as phone shipments rose under 2% — Arm is earning more per chip.
takeaways.title: Royalties keep climbing on Armv9 and CSS

takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was $410M, up from $22M a year ago, but a $290M loss from equity investments cut pre-tax income to $144M. A $66M tax benefit lifted GAAP net income to $210M, or $0.20 per share; excluding the equity loss and share-based pay, non-GAAP net income was $584M, or $0.55 per share.
takeaways.title: An equity-investment loss shrank the bottom line

verdict: Arm's revenue jumped 34% to a record $1,241M — its first quarter above $1 billion — as both license and royalty revenue set records, but a $290M loss on equity investments held GAAP net income to $210M, down 6% from a year ago.
